legend: Every flag below is attached to at least one row and is shown on the Flagged for Review page. A flag is not proof of wrongdoing — it marks something a buyer cannot confirm from the seller's own page and must resolve before paying.

flags.label: Weight not published
flags.what: The seller's page does not state the ring's metal weight in grams, so melt value cannot be computed and the price-per-gram test cannot be applied.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the weight before purchase. Without it, any price-per-gram figure would be an invention.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing for the weight in grams (and whether it is gold-only or total item weight). Keep the reply.

flags.label: Hallmark and/or maker's mark not published
flags.what: The page does not describe the stamp inside the band or the manufacturer's mark.
flags.why_it_matters: National Stamping Act (15 U.S.C. 297), summarised in 16 CFR 23.10, requires a quality mark on gold to be accompanied by the maker's trademark or name. A karat stamp with no maker's mark is incomplete.
flags.action: Ask for a close-up photo of the stamp before purchase; verify both the karat and the maker's mark.

flags.label: "18k" in the name, but not solid gold
flags.what: The piece is 18k gold vermeil: a gold layer over a sterling silver base. The seller's own spec says the 18k gold is a plating layer on recycled sterling silver.
flags.why_it_matters: 16 CFR 23.4 defines vermeil as a sterling silver base plated with gold of a stated thickness. A buyer scanning for "18k" could reasonably assume solid gold.
flags.action: Do not treat this as a solid-gold ring. If solid gold is required, exclude it.

flags.label: "Solid" is not stated by the seller
flags.what: The seller states the karat (e.g. 14K / 18K) but never uses the word "solid".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the listing to say solid gold explicitly. A karat alone does not rule out hollow construction, plating over base metal, or a two-metal build.
flags.action: Get written confirmation that the item is solid 14k/18k gold throughout, and that it is not hollow.

flags.label: Price is the setting only
flags.what: The figure shown is Blue Nile's "Setting Price". The centre diamond is priced separately, so the delivered ring costs more than the number in this table.
flags.why_it_matters: Comparing a setting price against a complete ring's price is an apples-to-oranges comparison. Any price-per-gram or melt test done on the setting price alone is meaningless.
flags.action: Add a centre stone to the builder and record the all-in total before comparing.

flags.label: Price not displayed on the page
flags.what: The product page as fetched showed no price for this item.
flags.why_it_matters: No price means no comparison is possible, and no price was invented to fill the gap.
flags.action: Check the price while signed in, or at a warehouse, and record it with the date and a screenshot.

flags.label: Return policy excludes precious metals
flags.what: Costco's official return policy lists "Precious metals are non-refundable".
flags.why_it_matters: This conflicts directly with your requirement that you can return the ring after inspecting it. Gold jewellery is a precious metal.
flags.action: Confirm in writing, for this specific item, whether a return is possible before buying. If not, this deal fails your checklist.

flags.label: Very short return window
flags.what: Wilson's requires contact within 7 calendar days of delivery, then the item must be shipped back within 3 calendar days of receiving the return label. Items are sold "as is". Cancelled orders are not refunded the 3% card processing fee.
flags.why_it_matters: An independent jeweller's assay or XRF test usually needs an appointment. A 7-day window can expire before verification is possible — the exact failure mode your checklist warns about.
flags.action: Line up the appraiser before delivery, or negotiate the return window in writing.

flags.label: Bank wire accepted as a payment method
flags.what: Blue Nile's return policy refers to refunds being issued back via bank wire or ACH, which means bank wire is an accepted way to pay.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist prefers a credit card for purchase protection and warns against irreversible payment methods. A wire is money you cannot claw back through a chargeback.
flags.action: Pay by credit card even if a wire discount is offered.

flags.label: Engraving voids the return
flags.what: Mejuri and Blue Nile both exclude engraved or personalised items from returns. Mejuri adds that free engraving is optional but makes the item non-returnable.
flags.why_it_matters: A free engraving can quietly convert a returnable ring into a final sale — exactly the exclusion your checklist tells you to look for.
flags.action: Skip engraving until after the ring has been inspected and verified.

flags.label: Large-diamond return is a credit memo, not a refund
flags.what: For diamonds of 1.00 ct or larger, Costco requires all original IGI/GIA paperwork and issues a jewellery credit memo after its own gemologist inspects the stone.
flags.why_it_matters: A credit memo is store credit, not money back. It also assumes you kept the certificate — so documentation retention is part of your return path.
flags.action: Keep every certificate and appraisal with the receipt from day one.

flags.label: Weight includes the stones
flags.what: The published weight is "total weight" of the finished ring, diamonds included. Gold-only weight is lower, so a melt calculation using this number is an upper bound, not the gold content.
flags.why_it_matters: Using total item weight as gold weight systematically overstates melt value — a classic way an otherwise honest calculator produces a wrong number.
flags.action: Ask for the mounting weight excluding stones, or accept that the melt figure is a ceiling.

flags.label: No independent assay or XRF result
flags.what: No seller in this study publishes a per-item XRF scan or an independent assay. The karat is the seller's own statement, backed at most by a stamp.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist's key point: a stamp proves nothing by itself. Every row here still needs post-delivery verification by an independent jeweller.
flags.action: Commission XRF or assay on arrival, before wearing or resizing.

flags.label: Unusual karat / not gold throughout
flags.what: This piece is stamped 19 karat — uncommon in the US market — and carries black enamel inlay, so part of the item is not gold.
flags.why_it_matters: 19K is 79.17% gold by definition, but an unusual fineness deserves an assay rather than trust. Enamel also means the item is not gold throughout.
flags.action: Have the fineness assayed; treat the enamel areas as non-gold in any value estimate.

flags.label: Verified at listing level only
flags.what: Price and material were taken from the seller's collection/listing page; the individual product page was not re-fetched in this session.
flags.why_it_matters: Collection pages can lag product pages. The figure is official but less durable.
flags.action: Open the product page and re-confirm price before buying.

flags.label: Product page not individually fetched
flags.what: The row's price comes from Blue Nile's official engagement-ring listing, which displays "Setting Price" next to each item.
flags.why_it_matters: The listing is an official source, but an individual item page is stronger evidence and may carry extra exclusions.
flags.action: Open the item page and re-confirm price, metal and exclusions before buying.

flags.label: Independent review research not completed
flags.what: Independent third-party reviews/complaints were not verified against a primary review source in this session, so no reputation score is asserted.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires independent review research. Inventing a rating would be a hallucination, so this is left open.
flags.action: Check BBB, Trustpilot and state AG complaint databases before buying.
